_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); hotel signals

pit_profile.why: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on franchising, management, and licensing, we own or lease very few of our lodging properties (less than one percent of our system)'; 'We are a worldwide franchisor, operator, and licensor of hotel, residential, timeshare, and other lodging properties under a portfolio of compelling brands at different price and service points'; 'As of year-end 2025, our system included 9,805 properties (1,779,936 rooms) in 145 countries and territories'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully for guests'; 'Our hotel brands and other lodging offerings generally compete with regional, national, and international chains that operate lodging properties or franchise their brands, lodging properties that are not affiliated with a chain, and online platforms that allow travelers to book short-term rentals of homes and apartments'; 'Economic and other global, national, and regional conditions and events have in the past materially impacted, and could in the future materially impact, our business, operations, financial results, and growth'; 'Changes in the way hotel rooms are booked could adversely impact our business'; 'In addition, the introduction of AI capabilities by existing and emerging travel intermediaries may change the way guests plan, book, and pay for travel, which may disrupt how our products and services are marketed and distributed, potentially eroding brand loyalty, increasing distribution costs, and negatively affecting our Loyalty Program, which could adversely impact our financial performance and our ability to grow our business' (its own FY2025 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it (the AI sentence of its booking-channel risk factor names a risk no theme in taxonomy_eras.json covers: GENAI is scoped to software, IT services, information, search, education and mobility, so it stays here, as home sharing did from FY2015)

BEAR.desc: EPS -29.4%/yr (worst year FY16-FY25 ex-FY20, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +11.4%/yr (Q3 fee guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY20 median

BULL.desc: EPS +14.9%/yr (FY16-FY25 ex-FY20 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +74.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY16-FY25 ex-FY20); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MAR (retrospective, 2026-10-09) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 1.94x (68.3% downside to Bear $116 / +35.3% upside to Bull $495) | Adj composite 2.48 vs market 2.38: gap +0.10 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +36% above the EPP floor $270 (23x FY26E $11.72) | Conservative 2-yr case: +5.1% total (+2.6%/yr) | At 31.2x FY26E the 15% hurdle price $484 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; North American RevPAR +6.7% in Q2 2026, forward fee revenue +10.16-10.84% (Q3 2026 fee revenue guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
